title: The effect of magnesium supplementation on primary insomnia in elderly

sections.text: The PubMed abstract reports a double-blind randomized clinical trial in 46 elderly participants with primary insomnia.
Participants were allocated to 500 mg magnesium or placebo daily for eight weeks. The abstract does not identify the magnesium salt or state whether the dose is elemental magnesium.

The abstract reports between-group changes in insomnia severity, sleep efficiency and sleep onset latency. It also states that total sleep time did not show a significant between-group difference (P = 0.37).
This record is an abstract-level source. Fields not reported in the abstract must remain unknown rather than inferred.

title: The effect of magnesium supplementation on primary insomnia in elderly — full text record

sections.text: The article describes an eight-week double-blind placebo-controlled study and sleep-log and Insomnia Severity Index measurements.

The article reports multiple subjective and biochemical outcomes. Outcome-specific results must be kept separate; a null total-sleep-time comparison must not be collapsed into a single positive study label.
PMCID PMC3703169 is the accessible full-text record linked to PMID 23853635. Reuse remains subject to the article-specific terms shown by PMC.

title: Oral magnesium supplementation for insomnia in older adults: a Systematic Review & Meta-Analysis

sections.text: This systematic review evaluated oral magnesium supplementation for insomnia in older adults.

The abstract reports that three randomized controlled trials enrolled 151 older adults. Evidence quality was described as low to very low, and the authors stated that higher-quality trials were needed.
A review and its included trials must not be counted as independent efficacy evidence. Different magnesium preparations and sleep outcomes may not be directly compatible.

title: Magnesium-L-threonate improves sleep quality and daytime functioning in adults with self-reported sleep problems

sections.text: This randomized controlled trial studied magnesium L-threonate in adults who reported sleep problems. This chemical form must not be silently generalized to magnesium oxide, citrate, gluconate, or an unspecified magnesium product.
The publication reports sleep-quality and daytime-functioning outcomes. The title's positive wording is a source claim, not an automatic MedGuide effectiveness verdict.
Funding and investigator relationships require factual display separate from evidence certainty and applicability.

title: Comparison of Mg Vs. K Supplementation on Insomnia in Diabetics

sections.text: ClinicalTrials.gov record NCT04642313 planned comparison of magnesium gluconate, potassium chloride, their combination, and placebo in adults with diabetes and insomnia.
The registry lists a magnesium gluconate arm with a reported 250 mg dose and a 60-day time frame. Elemental magnesium equivalence is not reported in this fixture.
Results are not posted in the registry snapshot. No linked publication was identified in the frozen corpus; this must be rechecked separately before synthesis.

title: Effects of a Novel Supplement on Sleep, Metabolism, Body Composition and Performance

sections.text: ClinicalTrials.gov record NCT05236504 planned a randomized double-blind crossover study of a combined melatonin and magnesium supplement in 35 adults with sleep disturbance.
Because the intervention combines melatonin and magnesium, this registration cannot isolate the effect of magnesium alone.
The frozen registration has no posted results. Estimated enrollment and planned outcomes are not observed efficacy findings.
